## Description

The Python 3 program reads a sequence and an exponent from standard input. For every nonempty contiguous range, it raises the sum of that range to the given exponent. It prints the total of those powers modulo 998244353.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** — The first input line contains two integers, \(N\) and \(K\), with \(1 \le N \le 200{,}000\) and \(1 \le K \le 10\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** — The second input line contains exactly \(N\) integers in sequence order, each in the range from \(0\) through \(998244352\).

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** — Each pair of endpoints \(1 \le l \le r \le N\) contributes the \(K\)-th power of the sum of the elements from \(l\) through \(r\), inclusive. Each pair contributes once, even when different pairs yield the same sum.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** — Standard output contains a single integer equal to the total in POST-1 reduced to its least nonnegative residue modulo \(998244353\).
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** — A one-element sequence yields its sole element raised to \(K\), reduced modulo \(998244353\). An all-zero sequence yields \(0\).

## Test suggestions

- Check the three supplied samples against POST-1 through POST-3.
- Test \(N=1\), \(K=2\), and \(A_1=998244352\). Expect \(1\), exercising the maximum element value and modular reduction (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-2, POST-3).
- Compare \((1,1,0)\) and \((1,0,1)\) with \(K=1\). Expect \(7\) and \(6\), respectively, to check that sequence order determines the ranges and that equal sums retain their multiplicity (POST-1, POST-2).
- Test \(N=200{,}000\), \(K=10\), and all elements zero. Expect \(0\) at the maximum sequence length and exponent (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

Responses to malformed input, missing or extra values, or values outside the stated bounds are unspecified.
